ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT obligations arise under Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and related Articles R.561-1 to R.561-63 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). Beneficial-owner identification and filing for companies are governed principally by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and R.561-55 to R.561-63 of that Code, together with Articles R.123-123 to R.123-125 of the French Commercial Code and the implementing framework of Decree No. 2021-1094 of 19 August 2021. Company formalities and beneficial-owner filings are submitted through the national one-stop shop operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or current commercial-register extract of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or company registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the country of origin is a Hague Apostille Convention contracting state; otherwise consular legalization through the issuing state and the relevant French consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current articles of association and constitutional documents of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company, notary, company registrar, or competent governmental authority, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or equivalent certificate of non-dissolution and legal existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign commercial registry or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate authorization approving the French SARL investment and appointing the signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board, shareholder, or other competent governing body of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization or certification under the law of the country of origin, followed by Hague Apostille where available or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each legal representative and declared ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a notary, lawyer, bank, or other accepted certifier, with Hague Apostille or consular legalization only where requested by the French recipient or the document-origin rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ownership and control chart identifying each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder and its authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed corporate declaration; notarization, apostille, or consular legalization if required by the filing agent, bank, or competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation formalities and beneficial-owner filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature certification where required, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of foreign-language corporate and identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French court-certified translator (traducteur assermenté) or translator accepted by the relevant French authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation attached to the authenticated source document; separate apostille is generally not required for the translation itself unless specifically requested

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, screen all founders, directors, managers, signatories, shareholders, UBOs, financing parties, distributors, and principal suppliers against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union consolidated sanctions lists, French national measures, and OFAC lists where there is a United States nexus. Apply French AML/CFT customer-due-diligence rules, including identity verification, ownership-and-control analysis, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth review for enhanced-risk cases, PEP and family/known-associate screening, adverse-media review, and documented risk-based escalation. Do not treat OFAC restrictions as independently binding on a purely French transaction without a United States nexus, but assess correspondent-bank and contractual exposure. Suspicious transactions must be reported to TRACFIN where the statutory reporting test is met.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; registry and company-name verification data are available through the Registre national des entreprises and Data INPI
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A French SARL name must be stated in its constitutive documents and filings using characters accepted by the French filing system. French Latin script is the normal format; accents and other French diacritics are generally accepted. There is no general statutory requirement to use French language or French transliteration, but the name must be sufficiently distinctive, must not mislead the public, and must not infringe prior company names, trademarks, trade names, domain names, or protected designations. A commercial name may be used in addition to the legal name. A legal-name availability search does not replace trademark, domain-name, unfair-competition, or regulated-sector clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a regulated banking, payment, investment, insurance, lending, or financial-services activity, including Banque, Bank, Assurance, Réassurance, Mutuelle, Établissement de crédit, Société de financement, Société de gestion, and similar expressions, unless legally permitted and appropriately authorized

Official state, public-authority, or governmental designations, including République française, Ministère, Préfecture, Autorité, and similar expressions, where use would create confusion or require prior governmental consent
Protected professional or regulated activity designations, including Avocat, Notaire, Expert-comptable, Commissaire aux comptes, and comparable terms
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, trademark, trade name, domain name, or protected geographical or institutional designation
Terms implying an authorization, public-service mandate, official certification, or government affiliation that the company does not hold
Geographical or international expressions such as France, National, Européen, International, or similar terms where the proposed use is misleading or subject to a specific protected-name restriction
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation mechanism with a universal 30-day reservation period. The 30-day period is an operational clearance hold recommended for the incorporation file, not a guaranteed legal monopoly. Conduct searches through Data INPI, the Registre national des entreprises, INPI trademark databases, EUIPO, domain registries, and relevant regulated-sector registers. If the Guichet unique, registry, or competent authority rejects the proposed name, obtain the written reason, correct the name or provide supporting evidence, and resubmit through the Guichet unique. A refusal of a formal administrative filing may be challenged before the competent administrative court within the applicable procedural deadline, generally two months from notification under Article R.421-1 of the French Code of Administrative Justice, subject to the notice and remedy information in the decision. A dispute concerning a prior private company name or trademark is ordinarily pursued before the competent civil or commercial court, with opposition or cancellation procedures available for trademarks.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SARL must have a registered office in France under Articles L.123-11 and following of the French Commercial Code. Domiciliation at a commercial domiciliation provider is permitted if the provider is authorized and the arrangement complies with Articles L.123-11-2 and following and the related regulatory provisions. A manager may, subject to statutory conditions and time limits, use a personal residence for domiciliation. A purely virtual address is insufficient if it prevents receipt of official correspondence, maintenance of mandatory records, effective management, or access by authorities. For a telecom-equipment OEM, a virtual office may be accepted for initial incorporation and administrative headquarters, but it is weak evidence of commercial substance where the company imports, stores, tests, certifies, sells, or provides technical support for routers and optical terminals. A real operating location, documented staff or outsourced functions, inventory controls, technical documentation, product-compliance records, customer contracts, and customs capability are recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official French statistical probability of unannounced inspection is published. For a newly incorporated medium-risk telecom-equipment business with foreign ownership, cross-border payments, import activity, and enhanced AML indicators, an internal planning estimate of 5% to 15% for an unannounced physical or documentary control during the first 12 months is reasonable, but it is not a legal probability or government forecast. Risk increases materially where the registered office is a mailbox, beneficial ownership is opaque, customs declarations are inconsistent, radio-equipment compliance is deficient, or tax and banking activity is disproportionate to declared substance. Relevant authorities may include the tax administration, customs administration, labor authorities, market-surveillance authorities, ANFR, and AML-supervised financial institutions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Livre II, Articles L.223-1 through L.223-43 (SARL); Articles 1832 et seq. of the Code civil; Décret n°2023-305 (Guichet Unique procedure); Règlement Général du RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; online filing administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) together with the Déclaration de constitution de société (M0/Cerfa), transmitted electronically to formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum: the by-laws may fix the share capital from €1.00. The full cash subscription must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the blocking attestation must be submitted with the incorporation file and funds are released only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions must be fully paid-up at subscription and valued by a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) when required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The founding associates of FR_SARL, having fully subscribed the share capital of €100 divided into 100 shares of €1.00 each, unanimously resolve: (1) Contributions are confirmed and the share capital is duly deposited into a blocked account for the company's benefit; (2) The registered office is fixed at the Paris address stated in the Articles of Association, and the manager is authorized to perfect the lease and related formalities; (3) [Name], French resident, is appointed sole manager (gérant) with full powers to represent the company, open bank accounts, sign contracts, and complete statutory filings; (4) Preliminary expenses are approved; (5) Submission through the mandatory Guichet Unique is ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel (avocat/notaire optional); no mandatory notarization unless real property is contributed; electronic signature permitted if provided for.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts containing the corporate name FR_SARL, legal form SARL, corporate object limited to ISIC 2630 manufacture of broadband cellular routers and optical terminals, share capital, duration (99 years), registered office, share transfer restrictions, management powers and appointment of the first gérant. All founding associates must sign every page and the final signature page; maintain a dated execution copy together with each associate's identity document.
required_dossiers: INPI corporate name reservation attestation (attestation de réservation)
Draft Statuts
Identity documents (national ID/passport) of each founding associate
Certificate of address for the registered office if not a lease yet
Declaration of beneficial ownership data for the register (RBE) draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is rejected for a formal irregularity (unspecified object, missing signature), execute a rectificatory collective act or publish an amending addendum signed by all associates and resubmit via the Guichet Unique without extra fee beyond the new greffe payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open temporary blocked capital account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank) or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-interest-bearing account in the name of 'FR_SARL, société en formation' at a French bank; transfer the full subscribed share capital; obtain the attestation de dépôt de fonds / attestation de blocage de capitaux issued to the future gérant, itemizing each subscriber, the share amounts, and confirming the funds are locked until registration. Deliver the KYC/AML file.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts
Identity documents of the future gérant
Bank KYC forms (source of funds, PEP declaration, corporate/entity questionnaire)
Final list of subscribers and amounts paid
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses or delays the account opening, remove the affected institution and repeat the deposit with another regulated bank; the attestation remains valid indefinitely and may be used in a later filing provided the sums are still blocked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal notice of incorporation in an authorized legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized to receive legal advertisements for the department of the registered office, on the list maintained by the Cour d'appel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Send the avis de constitution to the chosen JAL including the corporate name, legal form, object, registered-office address, share capital, duration, and names of managers; receive the justificatif de publication with the date and reference number. Verify that the wording matches the Statuts exactly.
required_dossiers: Draft avis de constitution containing mandatory legal particulars
Identity of the future gérant(s)
JPEG/PDF letterhead of the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publisher detects a discrepancy, ask the JAL to issue a corrigendum and a rectified attestation; any material divergence in published data must be covered before the incorporation submission to prevent greffe incoherence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Transmit the complete incorporation file to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) - Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); dossier transferred to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the secure national portal, select 'Création d'une société commerciale - SARL' and complete the electronic M0 declaration, uploading the Statuts, the blocked-capital attestation, the JAL publication receipt, the registered-office evidence (droit au bail/domiciliation agreement), the manager's identity and consent, associates' identity documents and the RBE beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the greffe registration fee online and keep the certificate of payment and the track-id (compte-rendu de dépôt).
required_dossiers: Executed Statuts (signed PDF or notarized deed)
Attestation de blocage de fonds
Justificatif de publication of the avis de constitution
Justificatif de jouissance du local commercial (bail, domiciliation contract or 3-months utility bill)
Identity document and signed consent of the gérant
Identity documents of all associates
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
Payment proof of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet issues a demande de complément, respond within 15 calendar days by uploading the missing document; after two failures the file is closed, in which case re-initiate the declaration and pay a new fee. Unjustified rejections may be appealed before the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS registration and K-bis identity extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the Guichet Unique travel; upon acceptance the greffe registers FR_SARL under a unique SIREN/SIRET and assigns the INSEE identification; the K-bis extract is then issued digitally, constituting the conclusive proof of legal existence; request the original K-bis for bank and contract counterparties purposes.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique file number
Receipt of payment
No additional document - the greffe draws from the transmitted dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis contains a typographical error in the corporate name, address, object or managers, file an 'inscription modificative' through the Guichet Unique with a rectification letter and supporting evidence; await the amended K-bis before relying on it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate definitive bank account and perform post-registration tax and social declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank; DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques); URSSAF; INSEE; Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present K-bis to the bank and request release of the blocked funds to the company's definitive account; verify automatic VAT number allocation by DGFiP; confirm URSSAF business registration; if the company opts for professional civil liability and business interruption cover, place the policies; perform the annual obligations (compte annuel, RBE update, registre des decisions).
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Bank attestation de sortie de blocage
Tax identification and VAT number confirmation
URSSAF certifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or INSEE numbers are not issued automatically, contact DGFiP (service des impôts des entreprises) with K-bis to obtain a duplicate; in case of delayed bank release, provide the RCS registration certificate to the credit institution; escalate to the Ombudsman if funds are withheld beyond 10 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (via DREAL - Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) for the ICPE site classification; Agence Nationale des Fréquences (ANFR) for radio-frequency equipment conformity (RED 2014/53/EU); Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) for industry policy and investment controls.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Attestation de conformité radioélectrique (Directive RED 2014/53/EU) and ANFR registration of the 5G CPE/router product; Récépissé de déclaration or Arrêté préfectoral d'enregistrement under the ICPE régime (Code de l'environnement, Livre V) for the manufacturing site; WEEE producer registration with an approved éco-organisme (SYDEREP) for placing electrical equipment on the French market.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL - Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement, under the Ministère de la Transition Écologique.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Electronics assembly (ISIC 2630) is generally a Déclaration (simple declaration with periodic environmental control) or Exempt under the ICPE nomenclature unless operational thresholds (e.g. rubrique 2860 WEEE treatment, 2795 organic peroxide/chimie, or VOC emissions > 20 t/yr) trigger Enregistrement or a full Autorisation requiring an environmental impact assessment report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the general prescriptions for declared installations (arrêté du 02/02/1998 for discharge and water emissions): pH 6.5-8.5, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/l, COD ≤ 120 mg/l; volatile organic compounds (VOC) governed by Directive 2010/75/EU and décret n°2017-838 with mass emission limits applicable to soldering/cleaning lines; hazardous waste (solder dross, flux residues, spent chemicals) must be tracked by bordereaux de suivi de déchets (BSD) and recycled via certified filières; WEEE must be reclaimed under the producer-responsibility obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Building permit (permis de construire) with fire-safety advice from the SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours); technical control certificates from an approved Bureau de Contrôle (e.g. SOCOTEC/Apave) for structural load, electrical installations and fire detection; ERT/ERP evacuation plan where applicable; establishment of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), registration with CARSAT for occupational risk and prevention, arrangement of occupational medicine (médecin du travail) at least every 5 years, and annual workplace inspection certifications.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), primarily through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Customs and import VAT matters are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through the douane.gouv.fr portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is registered through the electronic business formalities one-stop shop operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The filing generates or links the entity's SIREN and SIRET identifiers. The competent SIE assigns or confirms the French tax account and corporate income tax registration. A VAT identification number in the format FR plus a two-character check key and the nine-digit SIREN is obtained from the SIE. A non-resident foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the relevant non-resident tax service for a French tax number and, where required by taxable French transactions, a French VAT number. Importers must obtain an EORI number from French customs before customs activity. VAT registration may be required immediately for imports, intra-Community acquisitions, taxable French supplies, or an election out of the VAT franchise; the domestic turnover franchise does not prevent earlier registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. An SARL may elect for income-tax transparency (impôt sur le revenu, IR) if statutory conditions are satisfied, including the special regime for qualifying newly formed companies and the family SARL regime. The election is subject to eligibility, shareholder, activity, and time-limit requirements and is not a general U.S.-style check-the-box election. No general hybrid-mismatch entity election is available. Qualifying small companies may access the reduced 15% IS rate on a specified portion of taxable profit, while the standard IS rate is 25%, subject to statutory conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT/TVA), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT administered by French customs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the domestic VAT franchise applicable principally to supplies of goods, the ordinary turnover threshold is EUR 85,000, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500 under applicable rules. These thresholds are not a universal VAT registration safe harbor: imports, intra-Community acquisitions, certain cross-border supplies, and voluntary VAT registration can create registration obligations below the threshold. France also applies separate thresholds to services, generally EUR 37,500 and EUR 41,250 tolerance, subject to statutory sector and period rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice clearance system. Electronic invoicing between French-established businesses subject to VAT will be mandatory for receipt from 1 September 2026, and for issuance by large enterprises and certain designated entities from 1 September 2026. Small and medium-sized enterprises, including most SARLs, will generally be required to issue compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2027. Invoices must be transmitted through an approved private platform or the public invoicing portal under the final implementation framework. E-reporting of designated B2C and cross-border transaction data will be phased in on the same timetable. Existing invoice integrity, authenticity, data retention, and anti-fraud requirements remain applicable. Customs import and export declarations are filed electronically through customs systems and require appropriate EORI and declarant authorization.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced at 0% French VAT if the exporter can prove both the export transaction and the physical exit of the goods from the EU, normally through the electronic customs export declaration, Movement Reference Number (MRN), and exit confirmation or equivalent customs evidence. The exporter must retain commercial invoices, transport records, packing lists, order documents, and customs records. Services are generally governed by place-of-supply rules rather than a technical export zero-rating rule. B2B services supplied to a customer established outside France may fall outside French VAT where the customer-location rule applies; evidence of customer status and establishment is required. Input VAT refunds remain subject to normal deduction, documentation, and limitation rules. There is no French statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for applying the export VAT exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration containing the correct commodity classification, customs value, origin, exporter, consignee, and destination data
EORI number and customs authorization or representation documentation
MRN and customs exit confirmation, or equivalent evidence that the goods exited the European Union
Commercial invoice, packing list, sales contract or purchase order, and transport document such as bill of lading, airway bill, or CMR
Proof of delivery or transport evidence where required to substantiate the export chain
Import-country customs or delivery evidence where available
Bank payment evidence or accounting records where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a generally mandatory French export-VAT document
For telecom equipment, records supporting applicable Union product-compliance, classification, licensing, sanctions-screening, and dual-use assessments where relevant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export conditions or documentary proof are not established, the DGFiP may reassess French VAT at the applicable rate, deny or claw back related input VAT deductions or refunds, and charge late-payment interest. The standard late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Procedural penalties may include a 10% surcharge for late or incorrect payment, with higher surcharges commonly applicable for deliberate failure, abuse of law, or fraudulent conduct, potentially reaching 40% or 80%; a 100% surcharge may apply in specified obstruction or concealed-activity cases. False customs declarations may trigger customs duties, import VAT, customs penalties, seizure, and criminal liability. Intentional VAT fraud can result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under applicable French law. There is no automatic 180-day foreign-exchange clawback rule for French export VAT; reassessment is based on failure to satisfy VAT exemption, customs, accounting, or anti-fraud requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in conjunction with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the licensed supervisory body for credit institutions and investment firms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Articles 63–66, subject to EU-wide derogations and national security/statistical reporting measures. France imposes no blanket profit remittance restrictions; however, dividend distributions must satisfy French corporate law solvency tests and are subject to anti-abuse rules under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) if applicable. Capital inflows for equity subscription can be transferred freely into France, but must be reported to the Banque de France for external balance-of-payments statistics via the resident receiving bank. No prior administrative authorization is required for ordinary foreign investment, but investments in sectors listed under the French foreign investment control (IEF France) regime, including dual-use telecommunications infrastructure equipment, may trigger a prior approval requirement. For a 5G wireless CPE manufacturer under ISIC 2630, a pre-filing notification to the Direction générale du Trésor is required if the non-EU investor acquires control or a threshold of 25% of voting rights, assuming the SARL’s activities touch on France's critical technology perimeter.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not mandate any export proceeds surrender requirement or a compulsory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign currency or convert to Euro freely. All export transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 must be declared, through the intermediary bank (établissement de crédit), to the Banque de France for the balance-of-payments statistical collection under Regulation (EU) 2016/867 and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Articles R. 152-1 to R. 152-6. The declaration must be made within 12 months of the transaction, and the documentary evidence (invoice, customs declaration, bank statement) must be retained for 5 years for audit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium for treasury operational purposes (e.g., low-value supplier payments) under the ACPR e-money institution (EMI) regime or an EU passport from another member state. Offshore EMIs domiciled outside the EEA require full ACPR licensing and are not viable for capital escrow accounts. For statutory capital injection into a French SARL, a licensed credit institution (bank) is required to hold client funds and provide the capital certificate; an EMI cannot legally provide this capacity in France.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French anti-money laundering (AML) rules (Monetary and Financial Code Article L. 561-5 and ACPR guidance) require customer due diligence (CDD) before establishing a business relationship. For non-resident directors, most tier-1 banks demand an initial in-person or video conference interview (notarized for identity) and physical attendance for the authorized signatory is recommended, though remote boarding is permissible under the ACPR’s simplified processes if all source-of-funds documentation is electronically notarized (eIDAS-compliant). The final decision rests with the bank’s individual compliance committee; a minimum of 6-8 weeks should be anticipated for a foreign-owned SARL with a non-EU ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) in the telecommunications sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident non-EU UBO (e.g., Hong Kong or mainland China shareholder) with higher-risk jurisdiction flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Passport and proof of residential address for each UBO; (ii) corporate registry transcript in French or apostilled English translation; (iii) 3-month bank statements from the UBO’s principal bank evidencing legitimate source of funds; (iv) written business plan with confirmed purchase orders from French or EU telecom distributors; (v) sworn source-of-wealth declaration signed by the UBO; (vi) sanctions screening report (World-Check or Dow Jones) showing no adverse media.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product scope in 5G broadband network equipment (ISIC 2630) perceived as sensitive for national security
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Export control classification (EU dual-use Annex I) confirmation letter from French Customs (Direction Générale des Douanes) indicating that the router is not listed as dual-use; (ii) CE marking certificate and ANFR type-approval; (iii) internal AMR compliance manual; (iv) absence of sanctioned-party connection with telecom operators; (v) signed end-user statement certifying sales only to authorized French/EU distributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution through a direct SWIFT transfer from a third-country jurisdiction without prior correspondent bank notification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Pre-transfer notification letter to the receiving French bank including breakdown of the capital subscription (amount, purpose, UBO); (ii) certified copy of the shareholders’ resolution approving the capital increase; (iii) certificate from a French notaire or auditor (commissaire aux apports) attesting to the non-monetary contribution if applicable; (iv) bank account opening confirmation in the UBO’s name, not a pooled corporate account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or unclear operational treasury structure (e.g., intermediate treasury in a low-tax jurisdiction)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Group org chart with ultimate ownership and functional treasury roles; (ii) intercompany agreements and their transfer pricing documentation (BEPS TP chapter V compliant); (iii) business rationale letter for the treasury routing; (iv) if an intermediary entity receives funds, provide its audited financial statements and regulatory license.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The legal capital injection for the French SARL must be executed via SWIFT wire (MT103) from the shareholder’s corporate account to the dedicated escrow account at a French licensed bank. The wire must reference the following purpose: 'Souscription au capital – SARL [entity name] – [notarial/court registration reference]' and must include precise bank identifiers (IBAN, BIC). The French receiving bank will require a business purpose code (Code type d'opération) — commonly 'G0' for capital operations under the Banque de France nomenclature — and will submit the external balance-of-payments declaration to the central bank automatically. The sending bank must provide a copy of the payment order and the affidavit of the capital deposit from the French bank (attestation de blocage de fonds) before the notary or court can register the SARL. Inbound verification requires reconciliation of the SWIFT sender bank name (SWIFT BIC) against the UBO documentation, and the bank may request the underlying capital subscription agreement and shareholder resolution to satisfy Article L. 225-13 (SARL equivalent) and AML rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the CPE 5G router business will be conducted through two principal rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, customs duties, logistics fees, and general operational disbursements, using purpose codes 'R' (imports of goods) or 'S' (services) as per Banque de France reporting; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) for high-value raw-material or electronic-component imports from Asia (e.g., Chinese Wi-Fi chipsets and memory), with the French bank issuing at sight or at maturity upon presentation of compliant shipping documents. For inbound sales from EU distributors, SEPA CT inst or TARGET2 is used, but for non-EU customers, SWIFT MT103 remains the standard. The FR SARL should maintain a payroll and French tax payment rail via the commercial bank as well (DAS, DSN weekly).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) with an ACPR-licensed credit institution or EU investment firm under EMIR rules, provided the hedge is linked to a firm commercial invoice or supply contract.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for matched principal and interest flows under the SARL’s working capital facility.
FX options (plain-vanilla European) for purchase of USD trade payables, subject to forward validation of trade receipts.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for EUR-denominated use against freely convertible currencies (e.g., USD, GBP, CNY) because the Euro has full onshore convertibility; NDFs are reserved for restricted currencies (e.g., INR, KRW) and are not recommended. Only OTC products with ACPR-licensed counterparties are permitted; exchange-traded FX futures are permissible but must be cleared via an EU CCP.
Foreign currency savings accounts (e.g., USD savings) are permissible but are considered uncovered exposure and should be pre-approved by the bank’s treasury risk committee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval and filing of statutory accounts (AGM minutes and audited financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve annual accounts within six months of the fiscal year-end; the filed copy must be deposited with the RCS within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SARL: approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 4,000 for the legal person; court-ordered injunction with per-diem penalty (astreinte); repeated non-filing may result in administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale Form N°2065 / 2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SARL: filing no later than 3 May of the following year; if that date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deadline is postponed to the next business day. Non-calendar fiscal years: within three months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic increase in assessed tax, rising to 40% if the return remains unfiled 30 days after the first formal notice; late-payment interest accrues at 0.4% per month from the original due date.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) when, at the balance-sheet date, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover EUR 8,000,000; average permanent employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) under Articles L.123-13 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; EU-endorsed IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts of listed groups and is not the standalone statutory framework for an SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a standalone annual UBO recertification. A SARL must submit the register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) to the RCS upon incorporation and update it within 30 days of any direct or indirect share transfer altering beneficial ownership. The legal representative must also confirm the UBO data when filing any RCS update and at the five-year RCS data confirmation; failure to maintain an accurate UBO file may result in a fine up to EUR 5,000 for the legal entity.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – USD 600 per year for a professional domiciliation service; ordinary commercial lease costs are additional.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 15,000 per fiscal year for a statutory audit of a medium-size SARL, depending on complexity, headcount, and group relationships.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may qualify for a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. France provides tax credits and deductions for qualifying research and development, innovation, investment, apprenticeships, and certain energy-transition expenditure. Tax losses are generally carried forward without a statutory expiry, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and capped at the lower of the prior-year profit and EUR 1 million. The mandatory schema value of five years does not reflect the general French unlimited carryforward rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD corporate income tax return, with tax computation schedules 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and applicable annexes, filed electronically through the French tax administration's EDI-TDFC system or, where permitted, the impots.gouv.fr professional portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with corporate income tax installments generally paid quarterly or through four statutory installments during the financial year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year; an additional 15-calendar-day electronic filing tolerance is commonly available. For a non-calendar year, filing is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. Corporate income tax balance payment is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, financial year opening and closing dates, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French SARL as the taxpayer. Identify the French registered office and SIREN. Foreign shareholders are not substituted for the French taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, taxable result and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, applicable rate, gross corporate income tax, tax credits, withholding tax credits, and net amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include worldwide profits attributable to the French resident SARL, subject to treaty relief and foreign tax credit rules. Do not exclude foreign-related transactions merely because the counterparty is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling statutory accounting profit to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify non-deductible related-party charges, interest limitation adjustments, withholding tax items, and expenses lacking French business purpose or supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses, losses utilized, and remaining tax-loss balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% utilization limitation. Maintain schedules supporting losses generated before and after any ownership, activity, merger, or restructuring event.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits, and amounts carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by statutory conditions, contemporaneous records, and any required supplementary forms. Treaty foreign tax credits must correspond to qualifying foreign income and documented foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, capital gains and special computations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, capital losses, participation-related gains, depreciation recapture, and other special tax calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review asset transfers, intellectual property, intra-group reorganizations, and permanent-establishment issues. Apply French participation exemption rules only where statutory holding and accounting conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income and foreign tax credits claimed against French corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile each credit to foreign tax certificates, income categories, treaty provisions, and the French limitation applicable to the corresponding foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on interest paid to related entities and transactions relevant to interest limitation and anti-abuse rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border shareholder loans, cash-pooling balances, guarantees, debt pushdown arrangements, and interest paid to low-tax or related jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of tax credits, including research and development and innovation credits where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain technical files, employee records, cost allocations, subcontractor evidence, and project documentation in France or in an accessible form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and payment of the final corporate income tax balance after installments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment reference, bank mandate, tax account, and credit offsets reconcile to Form 2065 and the general ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Four installments generally based on prior-year corporate income tax, with a final balance adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Monitor thresholds, first-year exemptions, estimated current-year liability, and special rules for large companies. Recalculate installments after material acquisitions, losses, or tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information relevant to tax consolidation, group parent status, subsidiaries, and intra-group tax allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL owned by a non-resident parent does not automatically enter the French tax consolidation regime. Verify qualifying French ownership and election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent concealment or abusive conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month. Incorrect returns may trigger additional tax, interest, and penalties ranging from 10% to 80% depending on the taxpayer's conduct. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation can result in a penalty generally equal to the greater of 0.5% of the transactions lacking documentation or 5% of the reassessed profits attributable to those transactions, subject to statutory minimums and limits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VAT return Forms CA3 or CA12, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal or an approved EDI channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly or quarterly CA3; annual CA12 under the simplified regime where eligible.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The deadline depends on the assigned VAT filing schedule and is shown in the taxpayer's tax account. Monthly or quarterly returns and payments are generally due during the following month. Annual CA12 returns are generally due within three months after the end of the relevant annual period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French taxable turnover by VAT rate and output VAT due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate domestic sales, intra-Community supplies, exports, reverse-charge transactions, and transactions outside the scope of French VAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input VAT deductible on purchases, imports, fixed assets, and eligible business expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain valid invoices, import VAT evidence, customs documents, and proof of business use. Apply partial-exemption and non-deductibility restrictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: EU acquisitions, supplies, exports, reverse-charge services, and related statistical or recapitulative declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Validate customer VAT numbers, Incoterms, transport evidence, customs declarations, and consistency with EC Sales Lists and Intrastat filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late VAT filing or payment may result in a 5% surcharge for late payment, generally combined with 0.20% monthly late interest. More serious failures, fraudulent invoices, concealed turnover, or VAT fraud may produce penalties up to 80% of the tax, criminal prosecution, and joint or several liability in qualifying cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder is generally 25%, subject to applicable treaty relief. A 0% exemption may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France where the qualifying parent, holding period, subject-to-tax, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A 75% rate may apply to payments to non-cooperative states or territories or in specified anti-abuse situations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where relevant, and confirm the recipient's legal form and holding percentage. Apply the treaty rate only where French domestic procedural requirements are met, including any required Form 5000 and Form 5001 series or equivalent documentation. If withholding is initially made at the domestic rate, the recipient may seek a refund through the applicable French tax-office procedure. Maintain board resolutions, dividend vouchers, shareholder registers, tax residence certificates, ownership evidence, and anti-abuse analysis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents may be subject to French withholding generally at 25% under Article 182 B of the French Tax Code, subject to treaty reductions or exemptions and special rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%, depending on the agreement. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate lender is generally not subject to French withholding under domestic law, except for specific statutory categories, anti-abuse provisions, and payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, where a 75% rate may apply. Treaties may restrict or eliminate withholding and generally require residence, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse documentation. French VAT, financial transaction characterization, thin-capitalization, interest-limitation, and arm's-length requirements remain separately relevant.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million. Full transfer-pricing documentation requirements generally apply where the French entity or French tax-consolidated group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or belongs to a group meeting relevant statutory conditions. The documentation package generally comprises a Master File and Local File. A Country-by-Country Report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Even below the EUR 400 million threshold, the French tax administration may request evidence that related-party transactions are arm's length, and general transfer-pricing documentation and reporting duties can still apply.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods supported by the facts, functional analysis, reliable comparables, and French transfer-pricing principles
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the UAE ESR framework. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the French general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse standards, and business-purpose requirements. A French SARL should maintain genuine local management, premises or operational capacity appropriate to its functions, employees or outsourced resources under effective control, French accounting and banking records, commercial risk assumption, inventory and logistics evidence, and decision-making records. Conduit financing, royalty routing, artificial management, circular funds, and arrangements lacking economic purpose are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of sales, false invoices, dual bookkeeping, concealed cash receipts, fabricated expenses, or intentional misstatement of taxable profit or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax, late-payment interest, penalties generally up to 80% of the evaded tax, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions that may include imprisonment and substantial fines. Serious organized or aggravated fraud can attract enhanced criminal penalties and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, professional disqualification, tax-publication consequences, and civil or tax liability where their personal conduct or grossly negligent management caused the loss. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial arrangement, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL as a conduit with no genuine French activity, nominee management, circular payments, artificial royalty or interest flows, treaty shopping, or distributions to a non-beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization, reassessment of corporate income tax and withholding tax, 40% or 80% abuse-related penalties, late-payment interest, and possible application of the general anti-abuse rule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for mismanagement, tax liability in cases of fraudulent or deliberate conduct, and criminal exposure where false records, money laundering, or fraudulent insolvency is involved. Travel restrictions and imprisonment are possible only through applicable judicial proceedings, not automatically.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length pricing of imported routers, contract manufacturing, management services, IP royalties, guarantees, financing, or inventory transfers designed to shift profit from France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions, withholding-tax adjustments, interest, transfer-pricing documentation penalties, and penalties potentially based on 0.5% of undocumented transaction amounts or 5% of reassessed profits, subject to statutory rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for deliberate misstatements, obstruction, fraudulent accounting, or serious management fault. Routine assessment generally remains a corporate liability unless statutory personal-liability conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming input VAT on fictitious purchases, missing-trader transactions, incorrect intra-Community exemptions, false export evidence, or knowingly participating in a VAT chain designed to obtain an undue refund.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input credits or refunds, penalties up to 80% in aggravated cases, payment of interest, seizure, and criminal VAT-fraud sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, confiscation, and tax-liability proceedings where they directed, knowingly facilitated, or failed to prevent fraudulent conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party funds, disguising beneficial owners, failing to identify customers or suppliers, ignoring suspicious payments, or using trade transactions to layer or integrate criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting and supervisory sanctions, freezing or confiscation of assets, administrative fines, criminal money-laundering penalties, and possible prohibition from conducting business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face criminal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, management bans, and civil liability. The SARL must maintain accurate beneficial-owner filings and appropriate risk-based controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions, export controls, and dual-use telecom equipment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying 5G routers, encrypted equipment, software, or technical assistance to sanctioned persons, embargoed destinations, restricted end users, or controlled military or dual-use programs without required authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative or criminal sanctions, transaction nullification, asset freezing, confiscation, substantial fines, export-license revocation, and imprisonment depending on the breached EU, French, or international restriction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for intentional or negligent violations, including fines, imprisonment, confiscation, and management disqualification. Screening, end-use controls, classification, licensing, and record retention are required.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating customs value, misclassifying routers or optical terminals, falsifying preferential origin, omitting assists or royalties from customs value, or manipulating related-party import prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional customs duties, import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, delayed clearance, loss of simplified procedures, and potential criminal customs liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for intentional customs fraud, false declarations, or serious failures of customs governance, including fines, imprisonment, confiscation, and civil recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without approved accounts, distributing in excess of distributable reserves, disguising shareholder withdrawals as expenses, or paying dividends while the company is insolvent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, shareholder and director liability, corporate-law penalties, tax adjustments, and potential insolvency or criminal sanctions for misuse of corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may owe civil restitution, face management bans, contribute to insolvency shortfalls in qualifying cases, and incur criminal liability for misuse of company assets or presentation of false accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep statutory accounts, approve or file annual accounts where required, maintain supporting records, or report accurate ultimate beneficial owners and changes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court orders, civil fines, tax penalties, presumptive assessments, refusal of compliance certificates, and enhanced scrutiny of all tax filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face civil liability for mismanagement, fines, management prohibitions, liability for insolvency shortfalls, and criminal consequences where records were falsified or deliberately withheld.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating French sales, inventory, sales agents, installation teams, or contract manufacturing activity as foreign-only activity while failing to declare a French permanent establishment or resident business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive French corporate income tax, VAT, payroll and social-security assessments, withholding tax, interest, penalties, and possible permanent-establishment profit attribution adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for intentional concealment, fraudulent accounting, or deliberate failure to register and report French activities.
